header.running_head: Condemning Rulers who Live Lives Above the Standards of the Common People and who Veil Themselves from people in Need

blocks.text: punishment on his governors (when they deserved it) and whenever a complaint was brought to him about any governor, he would gather the complainant and the governor in one place. Thereafter, if the complaint was proven to be valid and the governor needed to be taken to task, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would take him to task. [^1]

Hadhrat Abu Khuzayma bin Thaabit (RA) reports that whenever Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed someone as governor, he would make a group of the Ansaar and some others witness (to the appointment) and say (to the new governor), "I am not sending you to give you sovereignty over the blood of people..." The rest of the narration is similar to the one quoted earlier. [^2]
The Statement of Hadhrat Umar (RA) Concerning the Duties of an Ameer

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent for Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir Jumhi (RA) and said to him, "We wish to appoint you in command of this regiment whom you should lead into enemy territory to wage war with them." Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) said, "O Umar! Please do not try me." Hadhrat Umar (RA) resolved "I shall never leave you. You people have cast this responsibility (of Khilaafah) on my neck and now you wish to leave me all alone! I am sending you with a group of people from whom you are not the best. I am not sending you to whip them or to humiliate them but only to lead them in Jihaad against their enemies and to distribute their booty amongst them." [^3]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once addressed the people saying, "The Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) has sent me here to teach you the Book of your Rabb, the Sunnah of your Nabi ﷺ and to administrate over municipal affairs." [^4]
